title: Launching a star
caption: A laser guide star launched from Yepun under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A powerful laser beam leaps from Yepun, one of the 8.2-meter telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT). Across the top of the image stretches the Milky Way, seen perfectly edge-on, with the galaxy's yellowish central bulge crossed by prominent dark lanes.

High in Earth's mesosphere, the beam excites sodium atoms, making an artificial star 90 km up. Known as the Laser Guide Star, it belongs to the VLT's adaptive optics system, which lets astronomers correct their images and spectra for the blurring caused by the atmosphere.

Those dark lanes are vast clouds of interstellar dust, impenetrable to visible light. Ancient Andean civilisations saw constellations in these dark nebulae, shaped like familiar animals, and one of them, the llama, is visible on the right. The VLT itself is made up of four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes, of which Yepun is UT4, plus four movable Auxiliary Telescopes, each 1.8 meters across.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by G. Hüdepohl. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the laser beam and the Milky Way's bulge may look brighter here than to an observer on the platform.
